summary: Weekly POC bench standup. Reviewed latency and throughput deltas vs Lyonexus' legacy provider. Identified routing and KV cache warmup as main drivers for p99. Discussed dedicated slot request and cost tradeoffs. Agreed on follow-up bench with hot KV cache and updated routing thresholds. Next steps: share configs, run targeted 100k token head-to-head, customer to share traffic trace and decision timeline.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-07-16 15:00 PT (41m) - Lyonexus bench standup
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Priya Natarajan (Redwood SE), Marcus Lee (CSM), Imani Ortiz (SRE), Tom Fletcher (Head of ML), Liam Chen (CTO), Sasha Ortiz (Infra)

[00:00] Jordan: okay everyone thanks for joining on time, we got 41 minutes scheduled, same agenda as last week quick readout on the bench numbers then tuning items and next steps
[00:14] Tom: great, yeah thanks Jordan, quick note Liam might have to jump out at 30 but should be fine
[00:20] Priya: awesome, i'll share my screen with the bench dashboard in a sec, i pulled the head-to-head vs incumbent provider from Tuesday runs, note that the runs are with the new quant profile and a conservative batch size
[00:36] Sasha: quick question before you dive in, those runs are cold start or warm right? last time we saw big p99 jumps on cold kv
[00:45] Priya: good call, these were mixed — about 60% warm, 40% cold, which I think is why p99 is noisy. i'll annotate which traces are warm.
[01:02] Jordan: high level numbers first? p50 p90 p99 and throughput per slot.
[01:07] Priya: yes so p50 delta is small: Redwood median is 6ms better on our test prompts, p90 we're +8ms, p99 is where incumbent still beats us by ~120ms on the mixed-run. throughput per dedicated slot on our setup is 220 tokens/s vs incumbent 190 tokens/s, so we have better raw throughput. unit cost per 1M tokens is roughly 14% lower on Redwood assuming steady-state.
[01:34] Marcus: those cost assumptions include the hot KV cache overhead?
[01:38] Priya: not fully, this is steady-state with prefix caching working; cold-warm scenarios change the tail.
[01:45] Liam: hmm that aligns with what we suspected, the tail is public-facing for customer latency SLAs. p99 is more important to our product than median.
[01:55] Sasha: when you say prefix caching are you referring to the kv cache? our infra team calls it the "K V cache" in traces, sometimes odd spellings in logs
[02:04] Priya: yes, kv cache warmup and prefix hits. we also tested a small LRU prefetch that helped reduce p99 by about 40ms in lab runs.
[02:17] Tom: can you explain the routing policy you referred to—latency first vs cost-first? last demo we saw Redwood route to a cheaper variant under heavy load which bumped tail latency
[02:28] Jordan: sure, the routing policy is configurable. currently our default for this pilot is latency-preferred, but we can set cost thresholds to allow fallback to quantized variants if throughput is saturated. in your runs it looked like some requests slipped to the cheaper 8-bit variant — that was the fallback policy kicking in.
[02:47] Priya: right, in one of the bursts the autoscaler hit capacity and routing picked 8-bit quantized variant on cheaper nodes — that reduced cost but increased variance in output and added latency for those specific requests.
[02:58] Sasha: did you capture a trace for the switch?
[03:02] Priya: yes i uploaded a trace link in the deck — link: https://redwood.app/bench/lyonexus/trace-20260716 (note: internal link).
[03:12] Liam: ok show of hands, do we want to prioritize p99 or push for lowest unit cost? i'm asking product side.
[03:21] Rita: from PM perspective p99—we can't degrade customer experience for cost.
[03:25] Tom: agree. we need consistent tails.
[03:28] Jordan: great, so target is p99 parity or better vs incumbent. let's make a plan: first identify what portion of p99 delta is from cold KV vs quant fallbacks vs scheduling.
[03:41] Priya: i broke the traces out. approximately 65% of p99 events are cold kv misses, 20% are routing to fallback quantized instances, 15% are scheduling spikes during autoscale.
[03:51] Sasha: that 65% is huge. can we warm the kv cache proactively?
[03:54] Priya: yes, we've been testing a pro-active warmup that replays the top prefixes for the day during low traffic. with that the p99 delta dropped ~90ms in one run. but it costs a bit of extra bandwidth and small compute overhead.
[04:10] Liam: acceptable if it keeps tails in line. what's the extra cost?
[04:14] Priya: ballpark 3-5% more tokens processed due to warmup, so unit cost delta is small relative to tail SLA benefit.
[04:22] Tom: can you run a dedicated slot config? earlier you mentioned dedicated slot request was an ask by us.
[04:28] Jordan: yes, we left one dedicated slot request pending. we can provision dedicated capacity with pinned GPUs to reduce scheduling churn. downside is higher reservation cost but much lower p99 variance.
[04:40] Marcus: reminder, dedicated also gives you isolation on noisy neighbors which affected your earlier tests on incumbent platform.
[04:46] Rita: what would the delta be for our expected QPS? we shared 120 QPS peak last week.
[04:52] Priya: for 120 QPS with batch size optimized and KV warm, you need roughly 6 dedicated slots by our estimates; with autoscale burst capacity for peaks it'd be 8. cost math in spreadsheet I'll send.
[05:05] Tom: i want to hear about security — logs, SSO, audit, KMS for keys. any red flags there?
[05:12] Imani: on private deployment we offer customer-managed KMS and VPC peering. for hosted we can bring-your-key via KMS and maintain audit logs. SOC 2 docs were shared last quarter — Jordan will re-send the compliance packet.
[05:26] Tom: ok that's good.
[05:27] Jordan: i'll re-share SOC 2 + network diagram after the call.
[05:32] Sasha: back to bench, can Priya outline the experiment we'll run this week to isolate cold KV effect?
[05:37] Priya: yes plan A: run a 100k-token head-to-head with two variants — one with proactive KV warmup (replay top 5k prefixes) and one baseline mixed warm/cold. keep routing latency-preferred with no fallback. capture p50/p90/p99 and token throughput. Plan B: run routing-config with strict no-fallback for 2 hours during peak trace to see tail under stress; Plan C: dedicated slot baseline run.
[06:01] Tom: will those runs include the quant extents? we need to make sure we test the same model family as incumbent to be fair.
[06:08] Priya: yes same model family, same tokenization, same prompts. the quantized variant is only used in fallback so we'll disable it for Plan A to isolate kv.
[06:17] Liam: timeline on results?
[06:19] Priya: i can run Plan A overnight and share results by Monday 07/19. Plan B and C take coordination with Sasha for traffic trace; target Wed 07/21.
[06:29] Sasha: i can provision production-like trace and hand it off today.
[06:33] Tom: perfect.
[06:34] Jordan: quick note on instrumentation — set tracer flags to capture 'route.decisions' and 'kv.hit' in logs so we can attribute p99 events. Priya will include sampling filters.
[06:47] Priya: also, we'll capture unit cost per 1M tokens for each run including warmup overhead so product can compare TCO vs incumbent.
[06:55] Tom: what about fallback behaviour under burst? is there a recommended threshold?
[06:59] Jordan: we typically set a latency threshold and a queue depth threshold; if latency exceeds X ms or queue depth > Y, route to fallback. for this pilot we'll raise the latency threshold to avoid quant fallbacks unless absolutely necessary — again because p99 is primary.
[07:14] Liam: are there any model quality regressions with the 8-bit quantized variant?
[07:18] Priya: small diffs in token probabilities occasionally, sometimes slight reranking changes on edge cases — not catastrophic but may be visible for high-sensitivity outputs. we'd prefer to avoid quant for customer-facing critical flows.
[07:30] Marcus: another idea: progressive rollouts where we route a small percent to quantized for non-critical traffic and monitor output divergence.
[07:37] Rita: sounds reasonable. we'll want an eval set for quality. Tom will own that.
[07:41] Tom: yep, i'll assemble a small eval set of 500 hard prompts and send to Priya.
[07:47] Jordan: great. any blockers from security or procurement?
[07:51] Tom: procurement asked for a basic SOW and pricing template.
[07:55] Jordan: we'll send a pilot SOW template with committed throughput and a month-to-month dedicated slot option.
[07:59] Sasha: on the infra side, i want to confirm peering and ingress rules for the test runs; i'll send the CIDR block later today.
[08:06] Imani: we'll need role-based access set up for logs and the console — RBAC mapping to your team leads.
[08:11] Jordan: noted. I'll include RBAC steps in the handoff doc.
[08:16] Priya: circling back to the traces, after Plan A i expect p99 to be within ~20-30ms of incumbent if KV warmup behaves as in lab.
[08:26] Liam: that's promising. if you can demonstrate that, we can push for dedicated slots in the contract.
[08:31] Jordan: ok recap and owners — Jordan will send SOC 2 + SOW + pricing and the cost delta spreadsheet; Priya will run the 100k token head-to-head and share p50/p90/p99 + cost numbers by 07/19; Sasha to provide prod trace and CIDR by 07/18; Tom to share eval set and confirm security stakeholders. Decision timeline target 07/28.
[08:54] Tom: one more Q — tests show better throughput per slot for Redwood. what's the risk of performance variance across regions?
[09:01] Priya: performance varies slightly by region due to GPU type and kernel optimizations; we recommend running a short regional sweep during Plan B. we'll include region tags in the run.
[09:12] Rita: ok let's do that.
[09:15] Jordan: anything else?
[09:17] (brief chatter)
[09:21] Liam: i'm good, thanks everyone.
[09:23] Jordan: perfect thanks all, we'll follow up with the deliverables. Meeting end.

Notes: occasional transcription errors in names (K V vs KV), timestamps approximate. Links referenced in call are internal Redwood bench links.
